title: From the Front a Tower, From the Side a Pagoda — Guangzhou's Zhenhai | China Travel Expert
description:
Look at it head-on and it's a tower. Step to the side and it reads like a pagoda. For 600 years this iron-red giant has watched over Guangzhou.

Zhenhai Tower (the "Sea-Guard Tower") was first built in 1380, at the start of the Ming dynasty, by the marquis Zhu Liangzu, on the hill in today's Yuexiu Park. It stands about 28m tall in five tiers, each smaller than the one below, with iron-red walls, green glazed tiles and upturned flying eaves — and when it was built it was the tallest structure in the whole city. Its grandeur earned it the name "the finest view in the south" (岭南第一胜览). Over six centuries it was destroyed and rebuilt five times; in 1928 it was rebuilt in reinforced concrete, keeping its old form. Today it houses the Guangzhou Museum, so you can climb the same tower and look out over the old city.

🧭 Expert Tip: Go up to the top floor for the view back over old Guangzhou — and give yourself time for the museum inside; the tower itself is the largest exhibit.
